baseSentence: The server responded to the ping request.
fullCorrect: The server didn't respond to the ping request.
translation: El servidor no respondió a la solicitud de ping.
trapExplanation: Al usar el auxiliar de pasado 'didn't', el verbo principal vuelve obligatoriamente a su forma base: responded → respond.

baseSentence: We push code directly to production on Fridays.

tokens.text: code directly to production on Fridays.

fullCorrect: We don't push code directly to production on Fridays.
translation: No subimos código directamente a producción los viernes.
trapExplanation: Con el sujeto 'We' (primera persona plural) se usa 'don't', no 'doesn't'.

baseSentence: You deployed the hotfix this morning.
fullCorrect: Did you deploy the hotfix this morning?
translation: ¿Desplegaste la corrección esta mañana?
trapExplanation: En preguntas en pasado usamos el auxiliar 'Did' al inicio y el verbo principal en forma base: deployed → deploy.

baseSentence: The test suite catches regression bugs.
fullCorrect: The test suite doesn't catch regression bugs.
translation: La suite de pruebas no detecta errores de regresión.
trapExplanation: 'The test suite' es tercera persona singular (it), por lo que requiere 'doesn't' y el verbo pierde la terminación -es: catches → catch.

baseSentence: The pipeline failed because of a missing dependency.
fullCorrect: Why did the pipeline fail?
translation: ¿Por qué falló el pipeline?
trapExplanation: Estructura Wh-: [Why] + [auxiliar did] + [sujeto] + [verbo base fail].

baseSentence: I write unit tests for every new feature.

tokens.text: unit tests for every new feature.

fullCorrect: I wrote unit tests for every new feature.
translation: Escribí pruebas unitarias para cada nueva funcionalidad.
trapExplanation: 'Write' es un verbo irregular cuyo pasado simple es 'wrote' (nunca 'writed').

baseSentence: She reviews pull requests before merging.
fullCorrect: Does she review pull requests before merging?
translation: ¿Revisa ella los pull requests antes de integrarlos?
trapExplanation: Con tercera persona 'she' en presente usamos 'Does', y el verbo pierde la -s: reviews → review.

baseSentence: They optimize database queries for high traffic.
fullCorrect: They will optimize database queries for high traffic.
translation: Ellos optimizarán las consultas de base de datos para alto tráfico.
trapExplanation: El modal 'will' siempre va acompañado del verbo en su forma base infinitiva sin 'to': optimize.

baseSentence: The API returned a 404 status code.
fullCorrect: The API didn't return a 404 status code.
translation: La API no devolvió un código de estado 404.
trapExplanation: No cometas la doble conjugación: 'didn't returned' es incorrecto; lo correcto es 'didn't return'.

baseSentence: You found the memory leak in the worker service.
fullCorrect: Where did you find the memory leak?
translation: ¿Dónde encontraste la fuga de memoria?
trapExplanation: El verbo irregular 'found' vuelve a su forma base 'find' al usar el auxiliar de pregunta 'did'.

baseSentence: She booked the flight to London yesterday.
fullCorrect: She doesn't book flights to London online.
translation: Ella no reserva vuelos a Londres por internet.
trapExplanation: Con 'She' en presente negativo se usa 'doesn't' y el verbo principal en forma base: book.

baseSentence: You have your boarding pass ready.
fullCorrect: Do you have your boarding pass ready?
translation: ¿Tienes tu tarjeta de embarque lista?
trapExplanation: Pregunta estándar con 'you': auxiliar 'Do' + sujeto 'you' + verbo base 'have'.

baseSentence: The hotel receptionist spoke fluent English.
fullCorrect: The hotel receptionist didn't speak fluent English.
translation: El recepcionista del hotel no hablaba inglés fluido.
trapExplanation: El pasado irregular 'spoke' debe convertirse en forma base 'speak' al negar con 'didn't'.

baseSentence: The airport shuttle leaves every twenty minutes.
fullCorrect: The airport shuttle doesn't leave every twenty minutes.
translation: El autobús de enlace del aeropuerto no sale cada veinte minutos.
trapExplanation: 'The airport shuttle' es singular (it) → requiere 'doesn't' y 'leave' sin -s.

baseSentence: They arrived at terminal two by taxi.
fullCorrect: How did they arrive at terminal two?
translation: ¿Cómo llegaron ellos a la terminal dos?
trapExplanation: En preguntas Wh- de pasado: How + did + sujeto + verbo en infinitivo (arrive).

baseSentence: I take the subway to the city center.

tokens.text: the subway to the city center.

fullCorrect: I took the subway to the city center.
translation: Tomé el metro hacia el centro de la ciudad.
trapExplanation: 'Take' es un verbo irregular; su forma en pasado simple es 'took'.

baseSentence: The airline lost our checked luggage.
fullCorrect: The airline didn't lose our checked luggage.
translation: La aerolínea no perdió nuestro equipaje facturado.
trapExplanation: Forma base de 'lost' es 'lose'. Con 'didn't', el verbo vuelve a 'lose'.

baseSentence: You pay tourist tax upon check-in.
fullCorrect: Will I pay tourist tax upon check-in?
translation: ¿Pagaré la tasa turística al registrarme?
trapExplanation: Para preguntar en futuro: Will + sujeto + verbo base (pay).

baseSentence: He showed his passport at the border control.

tokens.text: his passport at the border control?

fullCorrect: Did he show his passport at the border control?
translation: ¿Mostró él su pasaporte en el control fronterizo?
trapExplanation: Con 'Did', el verbo regular 'showed' pierde la terminación -ed y queda 'show'.

baseSentence: The museum opened at nine in the morning.
fullCorrect: When did the museum open?
translation: ¿Cuándo abrió el museo?
trapExplanation: Estructura interrogativa en pasado: When + did + the museum + open.

baseSentence: We attended the quarterly budget review.
fullCorrect: We didn't attend the quarterly budget review.
translation: No asistimos a la revisión trimestral del presupuesto.
trapExplanation: El verbo 'attended' vuelve a su forma base 'attend' tras el auxiliar negativo 'didn't'.

baseSentence: She approves vendor invoices every Monday.
fullCorrect: She doesn't approve vendor invoices every Monday.
translation: Ella no aprueba las facturas de proveedores todos los lunes.
trapExplanation: Con 'She' en presente negativo se utiliza 'doesn't' y el verbo principal pierde la -s: approve.

baseSentence: You sent the meeting invite to the client.

tokens.text: the meeting invite to the client?

fullCorrect: Did you send the meeting invite to the client?
translation: ¿Enviaste la invitación de la reunión al cliente?
trapExplanation: El pasado irregular de 'send' es 'sent'. Con 'Did', volvemos a la forma base 'send'.

baseSentence: The marketing manager agrees with the campaign deadline.
fullCorrect: The marketing manager doesn't agree with the campaign deadline.
translation: El gerente de marketing no está de acuerdo con la fecha límite de la campaña.
trapExplanation: Sujeto singular de tercera persona → 'doesn't' + 'agree' en forma base.

baseSentence: The project was delayed because of staffing shortages.
fullCorrect: Why was the project delayed?
translation: ¿Por qué se retrasó el proyecto?
trapExplanation: En voz pasiva usamos el verbo 'to be' como auxiliar: Why + was + the project + delayed.

baseSentence: They negotiate the service contract terms.
fullCorrect: They negotiated the service contract terms.
translation: Ellos negociaron los términos del contrato de servicio.
trapExplanation: Verbo regular terminado en 'e': solo agregamos -d para formar el pasado simple: negotiated.

baseSentence: He speaks directly with the regional director.
fullCorrect: Does he speak directly with the regional director?
translation: ¿Habla él directamente con el director regional?
trapExplanation: Pregunta en presente con 'he': Does + he + speak (sin -s).

baseSentence: The human resources team handles confidential reports.
fullCorrect: The HR team will handle confidential reports.
translation: El equipo de recursos humanos gestionará los informes confidenciales.
trapExplanation: El auxiliar 'will' siempre va con el infinitivo sin to: handle.

baseSentence: We reached an agreement during the second round.

tokens.text: an agreement during the second round.

fullCorrect: We didn't reach an agreement during the second round.
translation: No llegamos a un acuerdo durante la segunda ronda.
trapExplanation: Con 'didn't', el verbo 'reached' pierde la terminación de pasado: reach.

baseSentence: The presentation started at ten thirty.
fullCorrect: What time did the presentation start?
translation: ¿A qué hora comenzó la presentación?
trapExplanation: Pregunta de tiempo en pasado: What time + did + subject + start.
